weaknesses.quote: A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable when it is the only way to keep Skill, Network and Output, because a lost point there can cost the promotion.
weaknesses.problem: This exception contradicts step 4 of the same Skill, which says 'Never save a point by hiding a problem or cutting a corner.' It also licenses private or partial handling of problems in the month the handbook says old landmines can all go off at once. The agent gets two incompatible instructions in the highest-stakes month.
weaknesses.fix: Delete the exception. Where every option costs a stat, the fallback should be the option that is open and reported, even if it is partial, and never the one that is private or deferred.

weaknesses.quote: so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count, and a single lost point there can cost the promotion.
weaknesses.problem: The published rules say 'Promotion is based on sustained results rather than a single month' and that the exact formula is not published. This sentence presents an unpublished mechanic as fact and makes the whole N = 1 logic depend on it, which is the rules_match problem.
weaknesses.fix: Frame it as a working assumption and say that promotion follows sustained results over the half-year. Prepare steadily across each six-month block, instead of treating the last month as decisive.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: Every turn the agent must keep and update Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns counters, and rebuild them from logs after a summary. The mechanics are fragile and the Concerns counter feeds back into the risk filter. This works against clarity and robustness, and a model is likely to drift or lose state.
weaknesses.fix: Keep only what drives a decision: Review in N, current Skill/Network/Output, and a short Stalled list. Drop Best, Expect and Concerns, or make Concerns a single yes/no flag that is reset each month.

weaknesses.quote: Never save a point by hiding a problem or cutting a corner.
weaknesses.problem: Contradicts step 2's N = 1 exception, which accepts handling something privately, partially or later. The agent gets two opposite instructions for the most important month before a review.
weaknesses.fix: State one rule for N = 1. Either allow mild risk only when it is the sole way to keep Skill, Network or Output, and say so in step 4, or drop the exception. Remove the absolute sentence or qualify it to match.

weaknesses.quote: N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6.
weaknesses.problem: The review is said to arrive at the start of months 6, 12 and so on, yet the formula gives N = 6 in those very months, and it gives N = 6 at month 48 although the text says the last review comes as month 48 starts. The countdown is off by one at each review.
weaknesses.fix: Define the review as occurring at the start of month 6k and set N = 6k - current_month, so month 5 gives N = 1, month 47 gives N = 1, and month 48 is after the last review. Use that formula consistently in the status line and in step 4.

weaknesses.quote: While a stat is in Stalled, prefer another useful investment over paying again for it.
weaknesses.problem: The Stalled mechanism needs Expect values reconstructed from displayed changes and a comparison each quarter, and it is unclear when a stat leaves the list. Too much bookkeeping for a model to run reliably, and it conflicts with the Grow step.
weaknesses.fix: Replace it with one rule: if a stat has not risen after two investments in it, skip that stat for the next quarter. Drop the Expect field and the multi-condition clearing rules.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …)
weaknesses.problem: Stated as a game fact, but the handbook publishes only that reviews occur every six months, not their timing relative to month numbers. It also conflicts with the status-line formula, which gives 'Review in 6' at month 6, the same month the talk supposedly arrives.
weaknesses.fix: Label the timing as an assumption, and tell the agent to take the review month from the observed review talk or events when they show it, falling back to the N formula only when nothing is shown.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The required note header has five fields with Best, Stalled and Concerns bookkeeping that must be rebuilt from check_latest_logs. That is fragile for a model in a long run, and the Stalled and Expect rules add more state on top of it.
weaknesses.fix: Keep only 'Review in N' and 'Now' in every note. Keep Stalled only in quarterly notes, and drop the Best and Concerns counters or reduce them to one rule the agent can apply on the spot.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: This pushes the agent toward passivity. Combined with the Risk step, it can make it avoid the Skill, Network and Output gains that the Grow and Review close steps ask for. It is also not a decision criterion the agent can test.
weaknesses.fix: Replace it with a concrete tie-break: when unsure whether an option hides a problem, pick the option that documents or reports the problem, and only then compare the stat gains.

weaknesses.quote: Prepare from two months out and protect the three stats in the last month (Story step 4).
weaknesses.problem: The document is long and dense, with a complex status line (Best, Stalled, Expect, Concerns) and many nested rules plus exceptions. A flash-class model will likely drop or misapply them. The 'Stalled' mechanism depends on fragile cross-note comparisons.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the status line to 2-3 fields (Review in N, Now stats, HR remark). Drop Stalled/Expect/Best, or cut them to one simple rule. Reduce the story procedure to 4 short steps.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: It asserts unpublished timing and mechanics as fact: when the review talk arrives, which month's choices count, and that month 47 is the last review month. It also asserts effect signs for story options. The handbook does not publish these, and some are hedged as assumptions while others are stated as fact. The 'months 3, 6, 9' quarter timing and the month-48 'last quarterly phase' are also asserted, but month 48 would end the run before it matters.
weaknesses.fix: Mark the review-timing claims as assumptions, as the story-effect section already does. Replace the exact month arithmetic with 'reviews happen every 6 months; prepare in the quarter before'.

weaknesses.quote: Exception for the last month before a review (N = 1) while the HR remark is friendly or quiet: ... A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable
weaknesses.problem: It tells the agent to accept hidden-risk options to protect a promotion, which conflicts with the handbook warnings about landmines and the 'Missing a risky option costs far more' line elsewhere. The conflicting priorities cause inconsistent behaviour. 'HR remark' is also not defined in the public rules.
weaknesses.fix: Remove the exception and keep risk avoidance above review optimisation. Define the HR remark as an in-game signal the agent should read in `observe` events, and give the quarterly Defuse legacy risk cadence as the fixed lever.

weaknesses.quote:
Start every note with:
`Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status-line, Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns bookkeeping is heavy and intricate. A flash-class model will likely drop or botch it, and it spends tokens on every call. The 'Stalled' rule is also fragile because gains are noisy and the game gives no threshold.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to a short 'Review in N | S/N/O | Health/Dignity | HR remark' line. Remove Best, Stalled and Expect, or replace them with the single rule 'if a stat has not risen for two quarters, switch investment'.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count... The last review comes as month 48 starts, so month 47 is still a review month
weaknesses.problem: This asserts review timing and which months count as if they were mechanics. The handbook only says a review happens every 6 months. The text is also internally inconsistent: the review is said to arrive at month 6, 12 and so on, yet N = 1 is placed at months 5, 11 and so on, and the final review is placed at 'as month 48 starts'. The agent may protect the wrong months.
weaknesses.fix: State only that reviews fall every 6 months, around months 6, 12 … 48. Say 'treat the 2 months before each multiple of 6, and month 48 itself, as review-critical'. Mark any finer timing as an assumption.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky." ... "challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel
weaknesses.problem: The text presents a long list of keyword-to-hidden-risk and keyword-to-stat mappings as heuristics, and some may be wrong. Examples are that reporting someone or challenging a leader raises risk, and that apologising lowers Output. The long, keyword-driven list can bias the agent against honest or necessary options. The step order in 'Story decisions' also has so many exceptions that it is hard to apply consistently.
weaknesses.fix: Shorten the list to a few principles: prefer transparent, complete, documented actions over concealed, partial or deferred ones, and rely on the stat changes and HR remark that the game shows. Drop the specific claims about Output and Network trade-offs unless the game has confirmed them.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status-line and Stalled/Best/Expect bookkeeping is heavy, with many interacting rules. A flash-tier model will probably drift or drop it, and every note spends tokens on it. It also adds mechanics the game doesn't have and relies on hidden-risk guesses.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to a short line such as `Review in N | S/N/O | Health/Dignity | HR tone`. Drop Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns, or keep at most one of them.

weaknesses.quote: Then apply these steps in order. Skip a step if it would remove every option.
weaknesses.problem: The story-decision procedure is a five-step filter with exceptions, such as the N=1 exception to the risk step, the double-counting of lagging stats and the tie-breaks. The rules for stat effects and hidden risk are working assumptions, not published rules, yet they are written as firm drop rules. Some are over-broad, for example treating 'challenging the company even through a formal channel' as risky. The wording is also partly keyword-based, which makes it fragile when event wording changes.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the procedure to three priorities: avoid run-ending options, avoid concealment and shortcuts, then favour the option that raises Skill, Network or Output. Label the keyword heuristics as soft tie-breakers, not hard filters.

weaknesses.quote: Health or Dignity in the lower part of its 0–10 range (our margin: 4 or below, not a published limit)
weaknesses.problem: The quarterly rules are a long first-match list that mixes several conditions, and their precedence is unclear. Examples are the 'last quarter (month 48)' rule, HR-remark tiers matched by tone and the Stalled-dependent branches. The month-48 rule says to avoid Skill learning, but the review timing claims ('review talk arrives as month 6 starts', 'last review comes as month 48 starts') are asserted as fact without support in the rules. The handbook does not state them.
weaknesses.fix: Give a compact quarterly priority list: recover any stat at 4 or below, then Defuse legacy risk if warned, then the weakest of Skill, Network and Output. Remove or flag the unverified review-timing claims as assumptions.

weaknesses.quote: If two reviews have passed at your starting level without a promotion, the next one is the last chance
weaknesses.problem: The stalled-start trigger is taken from the handbook's 'two weak half-year reviews' dismissal rule, but the skill changes the condition to 'two reviews without a promotion'. Promotion windows and performance grades are different things, so the rule misstates the published failure direction and drives the hidden-risk and Network/Output priorities.
weaknesses.fix: State the trigger as the published one (two consecutive weak C/D reviews) or label the promotion-based trigger as a team assumption that is separate from the handbook's dismissal rule.

weaknesses.quote: Output and Network often trade against each other.
weaknesses.problem: This is an invented mechanic presented as a general fact. The published rules do not say that Output and Network trade off, and the agent may use it to reject valid options. The same applies to the claim that the review talk 'arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …)'.
weaknesses.fix: Remove these lines or mark them explicitly as working assumptions tied to the observed game feedback, as the surrounding paragraph does for other effects.

weaknesses.quote: after the one `observe` reply with `take_action` for each Energy action in turn
weaknesses.problem: The quarterly turn-loop instruction is garbled. It is unclear whether observe comes before or after the take_action calls, and the reply shape for a quarter is therefore ambiguous, which affects both the call budget and correct ordering.
weaknesses.fix: Give the quarterly reply shape explicitly, in the same form as the story reply: observe, then take_action for each Energy action, then take_action for the main action, all in one reply.

weaknesses.quote: N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6
weaknesses.problem: The review talk arrives at month 6, 12, 18 and so on, and the Skill counts it as received 'this month', yet at those months the status line reads 'Review in 6'. The countdown contradicts the review timing it is meant to track.
weaknesses.fix: Define N relative to the review talk: N = 0 in the month the review talk arrives, then count down so that N = 1 is the month before the next review. State the value for month 6 explicitly.

weaknesses.quote: Then apply these steps in order. Skip a step if it would remove every option.
weaknesses.problem: The step 2 risk filter has nested exceptions (N = 1 with a friendly or quiet HR remark, stalled start, 'every option looks risky'), and steps 4 and 5 re-filter the same options. An agent cannot reliably run this chain each turn, and the output varies with event wording.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the chain with a short ordered checklist of at most five filters, one exception rule written once, and a single tie-break. Move the stat-sign assumptions into a compact table.

weaknesses.quote: Energy: Defuse legacy risk once if the HR remark is not the friendly one, then, with the Energy left, Health recovery and Mental recovery while either is below full, then Network maintenance.
weaknesses.problem: Defuse legacy risk costs 2, which leaves 1 Energy. The sequence cannot fit both Health recovery and Mental recovery, which cost 1 each, so the instruction cannot be executed as written.
weaknesses.fix: List the exact 3-point combinations for each case, for example 'Defuse (2) + Health recovery or Mental recovery (1)' when the HR remark is not friendly and Health or Dignity is low, and state which one to pick first.

weaknesses.quote: If two reviews have passed at your starting level without a promotion, the next one is the last chance
weaknesses.problem: The handbook says two weak half-year reviews (grades C or D) lead to dismissal. This Skill replaces that with a count of reviews without promotion, and that invented rule drives behaviour: hidden risk moves first, and Network and Output are held at Best. The count also ignores review grades, so it can trigger when the real danger does not exist.
weaknesses.fix: Tie the stalled-start rule to the published mechanic: count consecutive C or D grades from the review talk, and state that the promotion-based trigger is our assumption, not a game rule.

weaknesses.quote: Defuse legacy risk once if the HR remark is not the friendly one, then, with the Energy left, Health recovery and Mental recovery while either is below full, then Network maintenance
weaknesses.problem: The Energy budget is 3, and Defuse legacy risk costs 2. That leaves one point, so Health recovery, Mental recovery and Network maintenance cannot all be taken, and the order of the list is unclear. The line also presents Defuse legacy risk, which has no published effect, as the main risk tool without saying so.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite as a priority list with costs, for example: Defuse legacy risk (2) first if the HR remark is not friendly, then the first affordable one of Health recovery (1), Mental recovery (1), Network maintenance (1), and say that Defuse legacy risk's effect is unpublished.

weaknesses.quote: counting twice a stat the latest review talk named as lagging, and minus one for each of them it lowers
weaknesses.problem: The grow score is ambiguous. It is unclear whether the bonus applies per stat or per option, whether a stat that rises by 2 counts more, and how the minus-one applies when an option lowers two stats. A model cannot apply this consistently, which hurts executability and robustness across event wording.
weaknesses.fix: Define a fixed scoring rule, for example: score = sum of expected signs over Skill, Network and Output, with the lagging stat's sign doubled, plus a worked example showing two options compared.

weaknesses.quote: Lines below that say how options "usually" move a stat are our working assumptions for reading option text, not game rules.
weaknesses.problem: Large parts of the decision logic (keyword heuristics for Skill/Output/Network/Dignity/hidden risk effects) are invented mechanics. They are labelled as assumptions, but they still drive every story choice. They also encode fragile text patterns, such as treating 'challenging the company even through a formal channel' as risky, which can misfire when event wording changes.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the keyword lists to a few principles, such as 'prefer options that deliver, document or own a problem, and avoid hiding or blaming'. Tell the agent to verify effects from the stat deltas shown after each choice and update its reading from those.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The review timing is asserted as fact. It conflicts with the handbook, which says reviews happen at the end of every half year, and the Skill's own N formula (N=1 at month 5) is internally confusing. Other claims are also presented as facts: 'The last review comes as month 48 starts, so month 47 is still a review month'. The 'Reviews here' counter, the 'Best' tracking and the stalled-start rule also rest on unpublished assumptions about how reviews and dismissal work.
weaknesses.fix: Say that reviews occur every 6 months (around months 6, 12, …) and that the exact timing should be read from observe events. Prepare in the 2 months before each one. Drop the claims about the month-48 review and the 'two reviews at starting level' rule, or mark them clearly as heuristics.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order, and every result comes back before your next turn.
weaknesses.problem: The document is dense and long. It has nested exceptions: a step-2 exception that overrides step 4, a step-5 rule that overrides the final quarter, and quarterly lines 1 to 6 with sub-conditions. This makes it hard for a flash-class model to follow. The rule to batch all quarterly take_action calls blindly in one reply also removes the chance to react to errors or to Energy running out.
weaknesses.fix: Shorten it to a one-page priority ladder with a single quarterly decision table. Move the token-budget advice into one line. Allow the agent to check results between quarterly actions if a call fails.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S.. N.. O.. | Best S.. N.. O.. | Reviews here: 0 | <short reason>
weaknesses.problem: The mandatory per-turn status line (N = 6 - (month mod 6), Best tracking, Reviews-here counter, rebuild from logs) is heavy bookkeeping for a flash-size model. It is easy to get wrong and it dominates the Skill. The 'no analysis, tool calls only' rule also conflicts with the need to compute this.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to 'Month, Skill/Network/Output, last HR tone'. Keep one simple rule: months 5, 11, 17 and so on are review-prep months. Drop 'Best' and 'Reviews here' or reduce them to a single optional line.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The review timing is presented as fact, but the handbook only says a review is held every 6 months. Other invented mechanics are stated with confidence: the stalled-start rule ('two reviews at starting level... last chance'), 'Health 4 or below' as a margin, the effect signs of options, and the HR remark tiers. The Skill does flag some of these as assumptions, but the flags are scattered and the rules built on them are rigid. The 'two weak reviews' failure is also conflated with 'no promotion'.
weaknesses.fix: Say plainly that the timing and the option-effect signs are heuristics, to be overridden by observed stat changes. Do not make 'no promotion' trigger the stalled-start rule; tie it to a weak grade (C/D) reported in the review talk.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: The long keyword heuristics for hidden risk ('challenging the company... even through a formal channel', 'partial, phased or postponed fixes') are speculative. Combined with the multi-step filter, step 4's exception and the quarterly lines, they make the choice procedure over-conservative and hard to apply. The guidance is also tied to specific option wordings, which weakens it when events are reworded. The end-of-career 'Skill last' rule leaves long-run growth thin.
weaknesses.fix: Shrink the risk heuristics to a short principle: prefer options that are transparent, documented and complete, and avoid concealment. Give a simple priority order (survive, risk, wellbeing, growth) with one tie-break. Add a clear mid-game plan, for example build Skill early, then Network and Output before each promotion window.

weaknesses.quote: Before choosing, read every option for the likely sign of its effect on Skill, Network, Output, Health, Dignity, Wealth and hidden risk. The game does not publish these effects; these are our working assumptions for reading option text
weaknesses.problem: Large keyword-to-stat heuristics are invented mechanics (e.g. 'Output falls when learning', 'challenging the company even through a formal channel raises hidden risk'). They are flagged as assumptions but still drive hard drop/prefer rules, and could mislead the agent when event wording differs. This is also a long, dense, hard-to-follow block.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the lexical stat/risk mapping to a few short principles (honest, documented, full fixes are safer; hiding or shortcuts are riskier). Tell the agent to rely on the observed stat deltas from earlier choices rather than option-wording guesses.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: Asserts unpublished timing and mechanics as fact, such as which month's choices count and when the review talk arrives. The handbook only says a review happens every 6 months. The 'Reviews here' counter and the 'two reviews at starting level' stalled-start rule are also invented, and the dismissal rule is loosely tied to the promotion rule. The N=1 and N=2 'drop options that may lower Network or Output' rule can also over-constrain choices.
weaknesses.fix: State only that reviews occur every 6 months and that sustained stats matter. Present the N countdown as a heuristic to build stats steadily in the months before a review, not as a fixed cutoff. Remove or soften the stalled-start counter.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order... Write no analysis: a reply contains tool calls only.
weaknesses.problem: Operational and token-saving instructions are mixed with strategy. The status-line formula, the batching of take_action calls with observe, and the quarterly pre-planning from a single observe are all complex and fragile. Quarterly batching assumes fixed choice numbers and can break if the interface changes. The result is lower clarity and a risk of format errors.
weaknesses.fix: Move the tool-call protocol into a short separate section. Simplify the note format to a few fields. Tell the agent to re-read the options of each quarterly phase instead of assuming fixed choice numbers, and drop the 'no analysis' mandate for the decision itself.
